change_note: Architecture 2 changed from Paper-Agent Committee to Minimal Virtual CSRP by explicit design decision before live comparative execution.
research_question: How do different forms and degrees of organizational specialization affect collective reasoning quality, evidence integration, and coordination cost in AI co-scientists for suicide-prevention research?

conceptual_axis.expected_strength: breadth of perspectives and explicit role differentiation

conceptual_axis.coordination_pattern: sequential research workflow with dynamic agent activation

conceptual_axis.expected_strength: lowest coordination cost and direct cross-paper integration
conceptual_axis.expected_cost: risk of insufficient functional decomposition on complex tasks

hypotheses.statement: The effect of organizational architecture on reasoning performance will depend on task information-processing demands; no architecture is expected to dominate across all task types.
The Functional Virtual Institute will provide the broadest explicitly differentiated analysis on complex tasks, but will incur the highest coordination burden.

Minimal Virtual CSRP will achieve a better quality–coordination trade-off than the Functional Virtual Institute on evidence-synthesis tasks by preserving distinct research functions while avoiding unnecessary agents.

The Shared-Knowledge Umbrella will achieve the lowest coordination cost and perform competitively on tightly integrated cross-paper synthesis, but may underperform more specialized architectures when tasks require explicit decomposition into distinct research functions.

Architecture performance will follow an architecture-by-task-characteristics interaction: the optimal level of specialization will increase with task complexity, uncertainty, and need for distinct analytical functions.

interpretation_rule: These are directional pre-pilot hypotheses, not conclusions. Null, reversed, or mixed findings remain informative.
